summary.text: Tina Kotek is the incumbent Governor of Oregon, a Democrat seeking a second term. She was a state representative from Portland from 2007 to 2022 and House Speaker from 2013 to 2022. As governor she has declared and repeatedly extended a homelessness emergency, signed a statewide shelter program, and signed a series of housing-construction bills.

paragraphs.text: Kotek moved to Oregon in 1987 and earned a B.S. in religious studies from the University of Oregon.
She later earned a master's degree from the University of Washington, which Ballotpedia lists as international studies.
Before running for office she worked as a policy advocate at the Oregon Food Bank and as policy director at Children First for Oregon.
Kotek served in the Oregon House of Representatives from 2007 to 2022 and as Speaker from 2013 to 2022, the longest-serving speaker in state history.
Her House Bill 2001 (2019) required larger cities to allow middle housing such as fourplexes.
She was elected governor in November 2022, defeating Republican Christine Drazan and unaffiliated candidate Betsy Johnson, and took office on January 9, 2023.

In July 2025 she signed House Bill 3644, which established an ongoing statewide shelter program with $204.9 million for the next two years, and later that month signed a package of bipartisan bills aimed at easing housing construction.
She advanced from the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary and is seeking re-election.
